thread:
sam: quick FYI — bringing up zephyrx-14b-int4 on canary. perf baseline looks okay but we get memory fragmentation spikes and intermittent OOMs on long generations when prefetch_window is large.
anya: do you have the canary numbers (GPU mem timeline, typical response lengths that fail)?
sam: on a canary pod: GPU mem climbs ~6.8GB -> 11.5GB over a long convo. fragmentation metric increases while active allocations are low. failures mostly when response > ~400 tokens.
zara: is this with async_prefetch + windowed batching? those two together have historically triggered kv-heavy fragmentation.
sam: config: async_prefetch: true, prefetch_window: 16, batch_window_ms: 8, default max_output_tokens: 512.
oliver: quick thought — lower prefetch_window and enable slot_reserve for cold starts. we saw similar with omega12b where prefetch heated up the free list.
jules: can you paste the OOM traces? want to see eviction vs allocation refusal.
sam: logs pasted:
```
[2026-03-19T15:12:31Z] alloc_gpu(1024MB) -> FAIL: fragmentation high, free_contig 50MB
[2026-03-19T15:12:31Z] KV cache grow_attempt -> queued; prefetch pending
[2026-03-19T15:12:32Z] OOM: new token allocation 2048KB
```
anya: free_contig 50MB — that's the tell. Not total free mem but contiguous slab shortage. We should avoid big single-request grows. Cap per-request growth or reserve a tail slab.
diane: propose controlled experiments:
- reduce prefetch_window -> 8
- cap model default max_output_tokens -> 256
- enable slot_reserve: 0.07 (reserve 7% of GPU mem for tail allocations)
- set eviction_threshold: 0.6 (eject earlier)
sam: ran a quick 4h canary with prefetch_window=8 + slot_reserve 0.07. OOMs reduced dramatically but 99th latency for short responses increased a bit.
zara: expected tradeoff. Could we do adaptive prefetch: small window for sessions that historically go long, or backoff after N tokens?
oliver: we already have hooks for session heuristics. Suggest prefetch_backoff_steps and a session-based window: keep initial window small until the session crosses 200 tokens. Config suggestion:
```
model_config:
  prefetch_window: 8
  prefetch_backoff_steps: 3
  slot_reserve: 0.07
  eviction_threshold: 0.6
  max_output_tokens_default: 256
```
jules: also try softer compaction of the free list — trigger a lightweight defrag pass after heavy KV growth rather than a full compaction. That reduced free_contig churn on theta experiments.
sam: concrete canary results (6h, ~50% traffic):
- OOMs down 92%
- 99th latency for short responses up ~12% (from 990ms -> 1110ms)
- cost delta negligible
anya: we need to check quality regressions from lowering max_output_tokens. Run the 50-sample long-instruction eval (summaries, code-gen long outputs).
diane: ran eval sweep with max_output_tokens=256 — truncation increased for long summarization cases. BLEU/ROUGE for standard tasks stayed within noise, but failure rate on long summarization rose from 3% -> 8%.
zara: tradeoff noted. Operational plan: use conservative defaults for hosted tier, allow Dedicated customers to opt-in to higher caps if they reserve capacity or buy Dedicated slots.
oliver: next steps I recommend:
1) Roll the above config to a 24h canary (prefetch_window 8, prefetch_backoff_steps 3, slot_reserve 0.07, eviction_threshold 0.6, max_output_tokens_default 256).
2) Implement session-based adaptive prefetch (window grows after 200 tokens).
3) Add graceful retry policy: on allocation hint fail, fallback to smaller prefetch and retry once before failing the request.
sam: I'll open a PR with the canary manifest and attach dashboards. tagging infra-bot for rollout scheduling.
infra-bot: @sam noted. canary rollout queued for when PR merges. will post deploy events and alerts. :gear:
anya: I'll run the long-eval sweep overnight and report metrics tomorrow. reconvene after 24h.
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
